พ.ศ. 2305 / ค.ศ. 1762 (ข้อเสนอจากแหล่งข้: B.E. 2305 / 1762 CE (proposal from local and government sources); B.E. 2479 / 1936 CE (ubosot)
หลักฐานของหน่วยงานด้านสิ่งแวดล้อมศิลปกรร: Evidence from an agency concerned with the conservation of artistic and cultural sites states that the temple was built in 1762 (B.E. 2305) and was originally called Wat Kongkha. Meanwhile, the Sirindhorn Anthropology Centre's archaeological database dates the key heritage structure to the ubosot built in 1936 (B.E. 2479). Its origins should therefore be read as a two-layer history: the temple's age according to records and oral accounts, and the age of the surviving building. These are not the same thing.
วัดตั้งอยู่บนที่ราบตะกอนริมคลองตะกั่วป่า: The temple stands on an alluvial plain beside the Takua Pa Canal, west of the waterway, in a town historically shaped by coastal administration, tin, and maritime trade. This urban context suggests that the temple likely served as a religious site for the riverside community, but no temple-specific evidence identifies its builder, the reason for its construction, or a direct role for Hokkien Chinese people or the town ruler. Details beyond the evidence should not be added.
อุโบสถที่สร้างใน พ.ศ. 2479 เป็นอาคารก่ออ: The ubosot built in 1936 (B.E. 2479) is a Southern Thai brick-and-mortar building facing east. Its stucco decoration depicts chedis, Buddha images, wheels of the Dhamma, and botanical motifs, reflecting its role as both a place for religious activity and a community craftwork of the late Rattanakosin period through the reign of King Rama VIII.
ประวัติวัดที่บันทึกในฐานข้อมูลโบราณคดีระ: The temple history recorded in the archaeological database says it was originally called Wat Kongkha before being renamed Wat Kongkha Phimuk in 1940 (B.E. 2483). At the same time, the ubosot and chedi remain in use rather than becoming heritage ruins detached from the temple. The differing names in the documents should therefore be retained so readers can see the site's development.
กรมศิลปากรประกาศขึ้นทะเบียนอุโบสถและเจดี: The Fine Arts Department registered the ubosot and chedi and defined the boundary of the heritage site in the Royal Gazette on December 18, 1996 (B.E. 2539). Registration protects the old buildings' value as artistic heritage, while the temple remains a Mahānikāya commoner temple with resident monks.
ทะเบียนสำนักปฏิบัติธรรมประจำจังหวัดของสำ: The National Office of Buddhism's provincial meditation-center register identifies “Kongkha Phimuk” as Phang Nga's meditation center no. 1, under a 2002 (B.E. 2545) resolution. The archaeological database currently says the site is maintained and generally stable and sound, but no evidence has been found confirming that it was affected by the 2004 (B.E. 2547) tsunami or specifying any period of abandonment or a restoration year.
ในข้อมูลที่เผยแพร่ล่าสุด วัดคงคาภิมุขยัง: In the latest published information, Wat Kongkha Phimuk still has resident monks and operates as a Mahānikāya commoner temple. The temple itself is identified as the maintaining body. The archaeological database lists the abbot, Phra Khru Nandapanyakon, as the contact at 076-421-479.
